# Exploratory Analysis of Bayesian Models

> An online book on exploratory analysis of Bayesian models and the Bayesian workflow: data visualization, prior elicitation, predictive checks, MCMC diagnostics, sensitivity analysis, PSIS-LOO-CV model comparison, variable selection, and communicating results. Examples are runnable Python using ArviZ with PyMC, Stan, Bambi, PreliZ, and other probabilistic programming tools.

Fitting a model is only one step. Practitioners also need to diagnose the quality of the inference, criticize the model against data and domain knowledge, compare competing models, and present results to a specific audience. This book covers those activities with numerical summaries, visualizations, and worked case studies.

Where to start: if you already have a fitted model, begin with MCMC Diagnostics, then Predictive Checks. If you are choosing between models, go to Model Comparison. For how the pieces fit together, read Bayesian Workflow.

Authors: Osvaldo A. Martin, Oriol Abril-Pla, Jordan Deklerk, and ArviZ-devs.

## Foundations

- [Working with DataTree](https://arviz-devs.github.io/EABM/Chapters/DataTree.html): Organizing posterior draws, predictions, and other outputs of a Bayesian analysis using DataTree structures in ArviZ.
- [Random Variables, Distributions, and Uncertainty](https://arviz-devs.github.io/EABM/Chapters/Distributions.html): Random variables, probability distributions, and how uncertainty is represented in Bayesian analysis.

## Checking Inference and Model Assumptions

- [MCMC Diagnostics](https://arviz-devs.github.io/EABM/Chapters/MCMC_diagnostics.html): Checking that sampling worked, using R-hat, effective sample size, divergences, trace plots, and rank plots.
- [Prior and Posterior Predictive Checks](https://arviz-devs.github.io/EABM/Chapters/Prior_posterior_predictive_checks.html): Testing whether model assumptions and predictions are consistent with the data and domain knowledge.
- [Prior and Likelihood Sensitivity Checks](https://arviz-devs.github.io/EABM/Chapters/Sensitivity_checks.html): Power-scaling sensitivity analysis to measure how strongly the posterior depends on the prior and on the likelihood.
- [Simulation-Based Calibration](https://arviz-devs.github.io/EABM/Chapters/Simulation_based_calibration.html): Verifying that the model and inference algorithm are consistent with each other using simulation-based calibration (SBC).

## Model Comparison

- [Model Comparison](https://arviz-devs.github.io/EABM/Chapters/Model_comparison.html): Comparing Bayesian models with PSIS-LOO-CV and ELPD.
- [Model Comparison (Case Study)](https://arviz-devs.github.io/EABM/Chapters/Case_study_model_comparison.html): A worked end-to-end example comparing several models, from fitting through LOO-CV to interpretation.
- [Moment Matching for PSIS-LOO-CV](https://arviz-devs.github.io/EABM/Chapters/Moment_Matching.html): What to do when Pareto-k values are high, including moment matching.
- [Model Comparison for Large Data](https://arviz-devs.github.io/EABM/Chapters/Model_comparison_large_data.html): Speeding up comparison on large datasets with subsampling and approximations to leave-one-out cross-validation.

## Building Models

- [Prior Elicitation](https://arviz-devs.github.io/EABM/Chapters/Prior_elicitation.html): Turning domain knowledge into prior distributions, with practical tools and examples.
- [Variable Selection](https://arviz-devs.github.io/EABM/Chapters/Variable_selection.html): Selecting variables in Bayesian regression models with projection predictive inference or BART.

## Workflow and Communication

- [Bayesian Workflow](https://arviz-devs.github.io/EABM/Chapters/Bayesian_workflow.html): How model building, checking, comparison, and iteration fit together into one coherent workflow.
- [Presentation of Results](https://arviz-devs.github.io/EABM/Chapters/Presenting_results.html): What to report and how to summarize posteriors and uncertainty for a given audience.
